title: San Diego dumps both Flock cameras and smart streetlights
gist: San Diego's city council voted to end contracts with Flock (est. $8.3B valuation) and Ubicquia, shutting down AI-driven license plate readers and smart streetlights after a council member flipped. Police cite a 20% decline in vehicle theft since 2023, but advocacy group Secure Justice says at least 513 Flock contracts have ended nationwide.

insights.claim: San Diego's city council voted to end its contracts with Flock and Ubicquia, making it one of the largest cities to drop Flock, a startup with an estimated $8.3 billion valuation.
insights.speaker: Ars Contributors
insights.so_what: Large-city churn is a revenue and growth-narrative risk for Flock.

insights.claim: The vote reversed the city's stance from three years earlier and followed council member Stephen Whitburn withdrawing support in October, which created a majority; Mayor Todd Gloria said he would not veto it.
insights.speaker: Ars Contributors
insights.so_what: Single swing votes can flip municipal surveillance contracts.
